situations.name: In-flight fetch supersession
situations.definition: A developer needs a late response from a superseded request not to overwrite the current view.

situations.name: Stale response guards
situations.definition: A developer fires an async fetch whose result may land after a newer one and needs the newer write to win.

situations.name: Number and cost formatting
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a count, currency, duration or percentage with locale-correct grouping and sensible compaction.

situations.name: File drop-zone ingestion
situations.definition: Accept files dragged onto a region and hand their paths to a backend ingestion or upload command.

situations.name: Windows WebView2 header race
situations.definition: Getting the IPC session token attached to a privileged call when the renderer fires it before the invoke monkey-patch lands.

situations.name: State transition validation
situations.definition: A developer expresses which status changes are legal and enforces them on write.

situations.name: Cancellation and teardown
situations.definition: Stopping in-flight work on demand: flagging it, killing child processes, letting metrics flush, and cleaning every registry entry.

situations.name: Data table
situations.definition: A developer needs a sortable, selectable, paginated table with loading and empty states.

situations.name: Publishing a domain event
situations.definition: Recording something that happened as a persona_event so triggers, feeds, healing and the UI can all react to it.

situations.name: Tauri event subscription
situations.definition: Subscribe a component to a backend-emitted event stream and unsubscribe cleanly across StrictMode double-mounts.

situations.name: Error boundaries
situations.definition: A developer needs a render crash to degrade gracefully rather than blank the app, and must pick a boundary flavour.

situations.name: Model and provider picker
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to choose a model (and provider, and effort) for a persona, use case, lab run, or A/B compare.

situations.name: Background polling lifecycle
situations.definition: A developer needs to poll a backend status endpoint on an interval, and must decide when it starts, stops, backs off, and whether a hidden window keeps paying for it.

situations.name: Entity health grading
situations.definition: A developer must reduce a pile of signals into a score, a grade band, and a coloured badge the user can act on.

situations.name: Log tail viewer
situations.definition: Show an auto-scrolling, capped line buffer of a background process's stdout that is not an interactive terminal.

situations.name: Period-over-period comparison
situations.definition: A developer needs 'vs. previous period' deltas from a time series and must not invent one when no prior period was fetched.

situations.name: Inbound secret provisioning
situations.definition: Generating, displaying, and letting the user rotate the shared secret that authenticates an inbound webhook.

situations.name: Sensitive clipboard handling
situations.definition: A developer needs to hand the user a secret (bundle bytes, share link, plaintext key) via the clipboard without leaving it there.

situations.name: One-time secret reveal
situations.definition: A developer needs to display a value that exists exactly once (a minted key, a pairing code) and can never be re-fetched.

situations.name: Atomic job claim
situations.definition: Taking exclusive ownership of a queued row / key so exactly one worker acts on it, even with overlapping ticks, multiple processes, or a restart mid-flight.

situations.name: Admission control and queueing
situations.definition: Deciding whether a newly requested run starts now, waits in a priority queue, or is rejected — under per-entity and global limits.

situations.name: Burst debounce and episode dedup
situations.definition: Collapsing a flood of near-identical signals into one action, and announcing a state crossing exactly once instead of on every occurrence.

situations.name: Source-derived codegen
situations.definition: A developer needs one language's artifact generated from another language's source so the two can never drift by hand.

situations.name: Deep-link into vault
situations.definition: Navigate the user from an unrelated feature to a specific vault sub-view (catalog, add-new, databases) to unblock a task.

situations.name: Bulk / batch command variant
situations.definition: Replacing N sequential IPC calls with one command that operates on a list of ids, and deciding what a partial failure returns.

situations.name: Lint severity posture
situations.definition: A developer decides whether a new convention lands as error (blocking) or warn (advisory migration) and how the existing ~10k-warning baseline stays non-blocking.

situations.name: Quantity display formatting
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a cost, token count, percentage, or duration so the same number reads identically everywhere in the app.

situations.name: Expand-in-place detail row
situations.definition: A developer needs a row/card that reveals its detail inline on click without navigating, and must decide what loads on expand.

situations.name: Navigation destinations
situations.definition: A developer adds a new top-level surface and must make it reachable, gated, tracked, and back-button-aware in a URL-less app.

situations.name: Schema-driven input form
situations.definition: A developer must render editable fields from a runtime-described schema (use-case input_schema, tool parameters, automation conditions) with defaults, samples, and validation.

situations.name: Local secret discovery
situations.definition: Scan the machine or a pasted blob for existing secrets, classify them to services, and let the user select which to import.

situations.name: MCP tool invocation surface
situations.definition: List a gateway's tools, build typed inputs for one, invoke it, and render a structured result.

situations.name: Entity relationship graph
situations.definition: Draw an interactive node graph of how entities relate, with layout, selection, filtering, and (in vault) revocation simulation.

situations.name: Entity switcher dropdown
situations.definition: Let the user search and switch among parallel entities of one kind (projects, conversations, twins) from a compact control.

situations.name: Date range picker
situations.definition: A developer needs the day-window control that scopes a dashboard's queries.

situations.name: Faceted filter bar
situations.definition: A developer needs the filter row above a list, ideally with a live count on each facet.

situations.name: List pagination strategy
situations.definition: A developer needs to load more rows than fit in one query — infinite scroll, load-more, or a hard cap.

situations.name: Threshold rule engine
situations.definition: A developer needs named thresholds that turn raw metrics into advice, alerts or badges.

situations.name: Dry-run preview
situations.definition: Executing a definition's validation and simulated effects without side effects, and rendering what WOULD have happened.

situations.name: Generate-preview-apply
situations.definition: A developer wants the user to describe intent, have an LLM draft a structure, review it, and commit it.

situations.name: OS notifications
situations.definition: A developer wants to notify the user outside the app window when a long-running process finishes.

situations.name: Enforcing an invariant the schema can't express
situations.definition: A developer needs a rule (range bound, exclusivity, cross-column implication) enforced at the DB, not just in Rust.

situations.name: LLM contract enforcement
situations.definition: Making the system behave correctly when the model ignores a rule the prompt stated — synthesizing the missing step, blocking bad output, or scoring it.

situations.name: Frontend test lane selection
situations.definition: A developer writes a test and must choose which of six runner configurations it belongs to, and whether any gate will run it.

situations.name: i18n key and value gates
situations.definition: A developer adds a user-facing string and needs every locale to have the key AND a genuinely translated value before it ships.

situations.name: Streaming CLI output
situations.definition: A developer needs to display live process/agent stdout with ANSI colour, search, and classification.

situations.name: Recording LLM spend
situations.definition: Attributing the token cost of a command-initiated model call to a source/persona/project so the spend ledger stays honest.

situations.name: Model-composed widget surface
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a dashboard whose layout and content an LLM emitted at runtime.

situations.name: Spend ceiling controls
situations.definition: A developer needs to expose the limits that stop an agent run from costing unbounded money or time — budget, turns, timeout, concurrency.

situations.name: Multi-source fan-out feed
situations.definition: A developer must assemble one chronological list from several independent backend queries, each of which may fail on its own.

situations.name: Bulk selection and batch bar
situations.definition: A developer needs checkbox multi-select across rows plus an action bar that operates on the selection and reports per-item outcomes.

situations.name: Version diff view
situations.definition: A developer must show what changed between two versions of a prompt, config, or output, inline and readably.

situations.name: Secret value handling in UI
situations.definition: Hold a plaintext secret in the renderer long enough to save it without leaking it into React state, DevTools, Sentry, or the persisted blob.

situations.name: Nested modal stacking
situations.definition: Open a secondary dialog on top of an existing modal without the Escape key or backdrop click closing both.

situations.name: Plugin connection setup panel
situations.definition: Build the gating first-tab of a plugin where the user establishes and tests a connection to the external system it wraps.

situations.name: Run history log
situations.definition: List past runs of a repeatable operation with status and a way to inspect or replay one.

situations.name: Next-run projection
situations.definition: Rendering the concrete future fire times a schedule will produce, so the user can confirm intent before saving.

situations.name: Manual test fire
situations.definition: A button that runs a saved automation once, right now, and reports pass/fail + cost + duration inline.

situations.name: Multi-step wizard shell
situations.definition: A guided flow with a step rail, per-step completeness, back/next gating, and (sometimes) resumption after the app is closed mid-flow.

situations.name: Raw definition JSON editor
situations.definition: Letting a power user edit the underlying JSON of a definition directly, with syntax highlighting, shape validation, and a safe path back to the structured form.

situations.name: Blast-radius confirmation
situations.owner: src/features/shared/components/overlays/ConfirmDestructiveModal.tsx (used by one caller in this slice)
situations.definition: Confirming a destructive or wide-reaching change by first telling the user exactly how many live things it will touch.

situations.name: Infinite canvas surface
situations.definition: A developer needs a pannable/zoomable spatial board with draggable nodes, links, and overlays.

situations.name: Shipped design variants
situations.definition: A developer explores several UI directions for one surface and needs to keep them switchable in the product while the winner is chosen.

situations.name: Closed-vocabulary value migration
situations.definition: A developer collapses two spellings of a status/category column onto one canonical set, without losing rows that match neither.

situations.name: Modal dialog
situations.definition: A developer needs an overlay panel with backdrop, focus trap, escape handling, and stacking.

situations.name: Tier-gated UI
situations.definition: A developer gates a feature behind a product tier and needs all three frontend bundles to still compile and tree-shake correctly.

situations.name: Deferred and idle work
situations.definition: A developer has non-critical startup work (prefetch, seed, cleanup) that must not compete with first paint.

situations.name: Relative timestamp
situations.definition: A developer needs to render 'how long ago' (or 'in how long') for a row, header or tooltip.

situations.name: Freeform JSON payload editor
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to hand-author a JSON input payload for a run, with parse errors surfaced before anything is dispatched.

situations.name: Session-scoped local persistence
situations.definition: A developer needs half-finished user input or a view preference to survive an unmount/remount that the user didn't intend as a discard.

situations.name: Secret reveal control
situations.definition: Mask a stored/entered secret in the UI with an explicit reveal, copy, and paste affordance.

situations.name: Entity audit trail view
situations.definition: Show the append-only operation history for one entity with filtering and paging.

situations.name: Idempotent send guard
situations.definition: Guarantee a user-initiated dispatch happens exactly once, even across double-clicks, retries, or an app restart.

situations.name: Sparkline
situations.definition: A developer needs a tiny inline trend line next to a figure, with no charting library.

situations.name: Bulk selection actions
situations.definition: A developer needs multi-row selection with select-all and batched accept/reject/delete.

situations.name: Master detail layout
situations.definition: A developer needs a list beside a detail pane, with a sensible mobile fallback.

situations.name: View state persistence
situations.definition: A developer needs the user's filters, sort, collapse and column widths to survive navigation or restart.

situations.name: Node-link graph canvas
situations.definition: A developer needs a pannable, zoomable node-and-edge visualization of a knowledge or pattern graph.

situations.name: Adoption questionnaire
situations.definition: Walking a user through a generated set of questions that parameterize a template, then projecting the answers into a concrete definition.

situations.name: Connector-sourced option list
situations.definition: Populating a picker's options by calling the user's own connected service at render time, including chained pickers that depend on a prior answer.

situations.name: Foreign definition import
situations.definition: Accepting an automation definition authored elsewhere — via file drop, paste, or URL — validating it, and previewing what was detected before committing.

situations.name: Unsaved draft persistence
situations.definition: Keeping in-progress authoring work alive across a remount, a route change, or an app restart — and deciding when it is too stale to restore.

situations.name: Partial-success bulk action
situations.definition: Applying an action to many selected items and reporting per-reason failure counts rather than a single success/fail.

situations.name: Impact-disclosure gate
situations.definition: Before a click spawns an agent that can write to the user's repo, the developer needs a gate that states impact class, ordered steps, and boundaries.

situations.name: Workspace export selection
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to pick exactly which entities leave the machine in a portable bundle.

situations.name: Demo data disclosure
situations.definition: A developer needs a surface to be explorable before real data exists without the user mistaking samples for their own data.

situations.name: Tier / plan gating
situations.definition: Refusing or degrading a command when the user's tier does not include the capability or has exhausted its allowance.

situations.name: Constraining an open text dimension
situations.definition: A developer has a free-form TEXT column that many independent writers fill, and must stop it fragmenting into a hundred near-synonyms.

situations.name: Boot crash recovery
situations.definition: Deciding, at app start, what to do with rows the last process left mid-flight so no work is lost and no dead work looks alive.

situations.name: Billing-account auth enforcement
situations.definition: Guaranteeing every spawned model process authenticates against the intended account, never silently falling back to metered API billing.

situations.name: Tooltips and hover help
situations.definition: A developer needs to attach explanatory text to a control or truncated value.

situations.name: Bounded parallel fan-out
situations.definition: Running N independent sub-tasks at once with a concurrency budget, isolating a panic in one, and collecting results in order.

situations.name: Audit logging a sensitive command
situations.definition: Leaving a durable record that a privileged operation happened, by whom, and to what.

situations.name: Structured logging
situations.definition: A developer needs a runtime event recorded so it survives to a bug report, without unbounded disk growth or a boot-order dependency.

situations.name: Prompt assembly
situations.definition: Building the full prompt for a run from persona config, tools, memory, connector hints, protocol contracts and mode directives.

situations.name: Autonomy gating
situations.definition: Answering 'may this autonomous action run right now, for this project?' before spending money or mutating state unattended.

situations.name: Event-name declaration
situations.definition: Naming a Rust→React event so the listener on the other side can be found and kept in sync.

situations.name: Grade and tier banding
situations.definition: A developer needs to convert a numeric score into a named band (A-F, elite/strong, high/mid/low) with a matching colour.

situations.name: Anomaly marker and drilldown
situations.definition: A developer needs statistical outliers marked on a chart and clickable through to a root-cause view.

situations.name: Connector slot binding
situations.definition: A developer needs a UI where the user declares which vault credential backs a given capability, environment, or project slot.

situations.name: Long-list virtualization
situations.definition: A developer renders a list that can grow to thousands of rows without dropping frames.

situations.name: Cross-database writes
situations.definition: A developer writes data that spans the app database and the user database, which cannot share a transaction or a foreign key.

situations.name: Model and effort routing
situations.definition: Deciding which model, effort tier and provider a given call should use, given persona config, policy, capability and per-use-case overrides.

situations.name: Keyboard shortcut registration
situations.definition: A developer wires a global key binding and must place it correctly relative to modals, palette, and nav mode.

situations.name: Vector KB ingestion
situations.definition: Load documents (files, directory scan, pasted text) into a per-credential vector knowledge base and track chunking progress.

situations.name: Diff and patch preview
situations.definition: Show a human exactly what changed between two versions of text or config before they commit to an action.

situations.name: Skill catalog and apply
situations.definition: Let a user search a library of reusable skills and either apply one to a live session or install it into a repo.

situations.name: Ghost row placeholder
situations.definition: A developer needs a skeleton that mirrors a specific row or panel silhouette while the first page loads.

situations.name: Unread and seen state
situations.definition: A developer needs to mark items as seen and surface a count of what is new.

situations.name: Alert rule editor
situations.definition: A developer needs a form defining metric, operator, threshold, severity and scope for a user-configurable alert.

situations.name: Status page uptime strip
situations.definition: A developer needs a horizontal strip of day cells or segments summarising a window at a glance.

situations.name: Definition version history
situations.definition: Generating a new version of a saved definition, previewing the diff/summary, accepting or discarding it, and reverting to an earlier one.

situations.name: Natural-language to definition
situations.definition: Turning a sentence the user typed into a pre-filled structured definition, with confidence and honest disclosure of anything the parser rewrote.

situations.name: Backfill window picker
situations.definition: Letting a user replay missed schedule fires over an explicit time window, with caps, future clipping, and a report of what was enqueued.

situations.name: Local/remote reconcile
situations.definition: Detecting that a remote-side object exists without a local record (or vice versa) and offering adopt / destroy / dismiss per item.

situations.name: Import conflict resolution
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to rule on incoming items that collide with existing local data, per row.

situations.name: Passphrase-gated secret transfer
situations.definition: A developer needs credentials to leave or enter the vault only behind a user-supplied passphrase, with the encrypted blob never leaking to disk unprotected.

situations.name: Scoped capability grant
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to mint a least-privilege, time-boxed token for an external caller.

situations.name: Entity creation form
situations.definition: A developer needs a create form with inline name-uniqueness feedback, validation gates, and side-effect provisioning on submit.

situations.name: Rate-limiting a command
situations.definition: Stopping a caller — or a runaway trigger — from invoking an expensive command in a loop.

situations.name: Concurrent-edit conflict
situations.definition: Handling two writers updating the same row when the second one's form was loaded before the first one saved.

situations.name: Zustand domain slices
situations.definition: A developer is adding new client state and must decide where it lives, how it composes into a domain store, and what its loading/error shape is.

situations.name: Persona visual identity
situations.definition: A developer renders an agent's icon, avatar, or sigil from a free-form icon string.

situations.name: Cloud-auth degraded mode
situations.definition: Deciding what a cloud-dependent command does when the user is signed out, offline, or holding only a cached profile.

situations.name: Markdown and rich output
situations.definition: A developer renders model- or user-authored text that may contain markup.

situations.name: Effective config resolution
situations.definition: A developer must show the value that will actually be used after a cascade (global default → persona → use case → run override) and where each level came from.

situations.name: Live log stream surface
situations.definition: A developer must render an append-only stream of backend output lines with classification, auto-scroll, fullscreen and copy, while it is still growing.

situations.name: Plugin panel shell
situations.definition: Frame a plugin's sub-surfaces in the shared content shell and switch between its tabs.

situations.name: Drag-to-move and reorder
situations.definition: Drag items within a list or tree to move them into a container or reorder them via a custom dataTransfer payload.

situations.name: AI-assisted connector authoring
situations.definition: Turn a plain-language request into a working connector definition (fields, healthcheck, setup docs) and iterate on it with the user.

situations.name: Voice input and playback
situations.definition: Capture speech to text through the user's chosen engine and speak responses back with volume and level control.

situations.name: Polymorphic config form
situations.definition: One authoring surface whose fields change completely based on a chosen kind (trigger type, binding kind, schema field type), then serializes to a single opaque config blob.

situations.name: Member roster & capabilities
situations.definition: A developer needs a list of team members with their roles/capabilities and per-member toggles.

situations.name: Comparison matrix grid
situations.definition: A developer needs a dense entity x dimension grid where cells carry status ink and open per-cell actions.

situations.name: Seeding built-in catalog rows
situations.definition: A developer ships default/catalog rows that must refresh on upgrade without clobbering user edits or deletions.

situations.name: Session resume and continuation
situations.definition: Continuing a prior model conversation rather than starting cold — for retries, healing, fix loops, or context carry-over between runs.

situations.name: Cross-artifact drift gate
situations.definition: A developer has two artifacts that must agree (Rust handler vs TS union, Rust events vs TS registry, error keys vs locale keys) and needs a check that fails when they don't.

situations.name: Secrets crossing the IPC boundary
situations.definition: Getting a credential value from the renderer into the vault (or keeping it from ever coming back out) without it sitting in plaintext on the bridge.

situations.name: Swallowed error telemetry
situations.definition: A developer has a background promise that can fail and needs the failure logged/breadcrumbed rather than silently dropped.

situations.name: Ranked top-N bar list
situations.definition: A developer needs a leaderboard-style list where each row carries a bar proportional to some denominator.

situations.name: First-use consent gate
situations.definition: A developer needs a blocking acceptance the user must give once before the app is usable, plus a way to inspect and reset it.

situations.name: Cross-store communication
situations.definition: A developer needs one domain store to react to, or read from, another without importing it directly.

situations.name: In-page tab strip
situations.definition: A developer needs to switch between sibling views inside a page.

situations.name: Tables
situations.definition: A developer needs a data table with loading, empty, and row-entrance behaviour.

situations.name: Connector catalog browse
situations.definition: Present the full connector catalog as a filterable, searchable grid so the user can pick what to connect.

situations.name: Backend token to remediation
situations.definition: Turn a language-agnostic backend status token into a localized label plus a concrete 'here is how to fix it' line.

situations.name: Queue-walking detail modal
situations.definition: A developer needs prev/next navigation inside a detail modal over the list the user opened it from.

situations.name: Untyped payload normalization
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a free-form JSON/text blob whose shape varies by producer.

situations.name: Streaming generation session
situations.definition: Driving a long backend/LLM job from the UI with live log lines, phase transitions, cancellation, and recovery if the view unmounts or the app restarts.

situations.name: Keyed rate limiting
situations.definition: Capping how often an operation may run per key over a sliding window, and telling the caller when to retry.

situations.name: Warm session and result caching
situations.definition: Avoiding repeated setup cost by keeping a subprocess, session, or prepared payload alive between calls, with correct invalidation.

situations.name: Agent workspace isolation
situations.definition: Giving an agent run a working directory and a way to undo what it did there, without letting it reach outside.

situations.name: Entity visual identity
situations.definition: A developer needs a persona/connector rendered as an icon + colour, consistently, in a row, a chip, a modal, and a canvas.

situations.name: Compile-time env embedding
situations.definition: A developer needs a build-time constant (OAuth client id, Sentry DSN, Supabase key) baked into the shipped binary from .env.

situations.name: Modals
situations.definition: A developer needs a focus-trapped overlay dialog.

situations.name: Toasts and transient feedback
situations.definition: A developer needs to tell the user that something just succeeded or failed, without blocking them.

situations.name: List view state
situations.definition: A developer needs search + status/health/tag filters + sort + grouping over a collection, kept consistent with the rows actually shown.

situations.name: Dashboard filter scope
situations.definition: A developer needs persona and time-window filters shared across sibling tabs, and must keep clear which panes actually honour them.

situations.name: Expandable disclosure row
situations.definition: A developer needs a row that expands into a detail panel, sometimes fetching its contents on expand.

situations.name: Tab strips and view switching
situations.definition: A developer needs to switch between sub-views inside a page or panel.

situations.name: TTL-cached read command
situations.definition: Avoiding a repeated expensive computation when the UI polls a read command on mount and after every mutation.

situations.name: Scheduled trigger firing
situations.definition: Evaluating cron/interval schedules on a tick and publishing exactly the right fires, including catching up slots missed while the app was closed.

situations.name: Duplicated CI systems
situations.definition: A developer adds or changes a gate and must decide whether the second, parallel CI definition also needs it.

situations.name: Span tree and waterfall
situations.definition: A developer must render a nested trace (spans, subagents, chain steps) as a collapsible tree with a proportional timeline and per-node cost.

situations.name: Per-entity event subscription
situations.definition: Let the user turn platform events on or off for one entity and configure each event's parameters inline.

situations.name: Token and cost rollup
situations.definition: Aggregate LLM token, cache, and spend numbers into a glanceable summary at session and fleet granularity.

situations.name: Narrowed filter detection
situations.definition: A developer needs to know whether the user has actually narrowed the view, to pick between 'all clear' and 'no matches'.

situations.name: LLM output fallback chain
situations.definition: A developer needs a surface that degrades from model-composed to deterministic to honest-quiet when generation fails or has nothing to say.

situations.name: Virtualized list
situations.definition: A developer needs a long list to render only visible rows while keeping grouping and entrance animation intact.

situations.name: Live session terminal
situations.definition: A developer needs to show a running agent session's output inside a feature surface and let the user reply to it.

situations.name: Streaming output rendering
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a token-by-token agent stream without re-rendering the whole surface per chunk.

situations.name: Settings change audit
situations.definition: A developer changing a setting needs the change recorded and surfaced back to the user as history.

situations.name: Dedupe then add a unique index
situations.definition: A developer wants to enforce uniqueness on a column that already contains duplicates in shipped databases.

situations.name: Model invariant contracts
situations.definition: A developer documents a load-bearing rule about a table that no type or constraint can express, and points at what enforces it.

situations.name: Ordering and reordering rows
situations.definition: A developer persists a user-controlled display order and applies a drag-and-drop reorder.

situations.name: Bundling native assets
situations.definition: A developer ships a non-Rust artifact (ONNX runtime, skill files, models, icons) with the installer and must guarantee the app can find it at runtime.

situations.name: Typed error taxonomy
situations.definition: A developer needs to add or classify a fallible outcome so it crosses the IPC boundary as a structured, categorized, machine-branchable error rather than a string.

situations.name: App settings read/write
situations.definition: A developer needs a durable, backend-stored preference readable from any panel.

situations.name: Metric tile
situations.definition: A developer needs a single labeled figure with an icon, optional trend and sparkline, rendered consistently across a dashboard.

situations.name: Decision and approval rows
situations.definition: A developer builds a surface where the user accepts/rejects a stream of proposals.

situations.name: OAuth connect flow
situations.definition: Kick off a provider consent handshake, poll for completion, and land a token reference on the credential without token material crossing IPC.

situations.name: Wizard with gated steps
situations.definition: Walk a user through a fixed ordered sequence of setup steps with per-step validation and a progress rail.

situations.name: Credential rotation policy
situations.definition: Configure a rotation schedule for a credential, show the countdown, and expose rotate-now plus rotation history.

situations.name: Findings triage queue
situations.definition: Route an auto-raised finding to an autonomous runner or an interactive session, with provenance and later verification.

situations.name: Quick-start palette
situations.definition: Offering a curated set of pre-filled starting points (templates, presets, quick ranges, canned test cases) that seed a form instead of starting blank.

situations.name: Agent-declared UI
situations.definition: A developer wants a persona run to emit interactive UI rather than prose, without letting a model inject arbitrary markup.

situations.name: Dispatching work to an agent
situations.definition: A developer builds a surface that hands a prepared prompt to an agent and must get user consent about transport.

situations.name: Credential injection into a child
situations.definition: Getting a decrypted secret out of the vault and into a spawned process's environment safely, refreshing OAuth first if needed.

situations.name: Master key sourcing policy
situations.definition: A developer is deciding where the 32-byte encryption key comes from on a given platform and what happens when the OS keychain is unavailable.

situations.name: Direct external API client
situations.definition: Call a third-party HTTP API straight from the renderer with a timeout, a caller abort signal, and typed errors.

situations.name: Local model install
situations.definition: Download and install an on-device model or sidecar binary with a progress bar, cancel, and failure state.

situations.name: Webhook request inspector
situations.definition: Showing the raw inbound requests an endpoint received, with headers/body, the resulting event, and replay / copy-as-cURL affordances.

situations.name: Rate-limit controls
situations.definition: Authoring throttle policy (max per window, cooldown, max concurrent) and showing the live runtime state against it.

situations.name: Attention counts and badges
situations.definition: A developer adds a domain whose 'items needing action' count must show up on the sidebar, a tab, or a dashboard header.

situations.name: Scroll affordances
situations.definition: A developer has a scrollable region and needs edge shadows, position restoration, or infinite-scroll triggering.

situations.name: Installer acceptance testing
situations.definition: A developer needs proof that the packaged installer actually installs, launches, and finds its runtime deps on a clean machine.

situations.name: Live PTY terminal viewer
situations.definition: Attach a durable streaming terminal to a running CLI process so scrollback survives unmount and remount.

situations.name: Rate metric identity
situations.definition: A developer needs to render a percentage (success rate, uptime) and must pin down which numerator, denominator, source and time window it means.

situations.name: First-run onboarding flow
situations.definition: A developer needs a gated multi-step first-launch sequence that lands the user on a working artifact.

situations.name: Provider failover
situations.definition: Detecting a retryable provider failure and moving the same run to the next model/provider candidate without failing it.

situations.name: Healing strategy selection
situations.definition: Choosing what happens after a run fails: retry with backoff, resume the session and let the model fix itself, roll back, or disable the persona.

situations.name: Event to subscriber matching
situations.definition: Deciding which personas/triggers a published event should wake, and recording why a match did NOT produce a run.

situations.name: Durable terminal-state persistence
situations.definition: Writing an operation's final status so it is never lost, never overwrites a status a racing path already wrote, and dead-letters if the DB is unavailable.

situations.name: Telemetry scrubbing and opt-in
situations.definition: A developer needs a crash or error reported to Sentry without shipping PII, credentials, or debug-build noise.

situations.name: Query performance instrumentation
situations.definition: A developer wants a new repository function's latency visible in the slow-query surface.

situations.name: Settings panel scaffold
situations.definition: A developer adding a new settings tab needs the canonical multi-section panel shape: header, quick-nav rail, section cards, scroll-spy.

situations.name: Usage analytics
situations.definition: A developer wants a feature's usage, activation milestone, or conversion tracked without leaking user content.

situations.name: Dev-only diagnostics
situations.definition: A developer wants an in-app tool (inspector, freeze watchdog, store monitor, IPC metrics) that must be fully absent from production builds.

situations.name: Document signing and verification
situations.definition: Cryptographically sign a file, write or import a sidecar signature, and verify a file against it.

situations.name: Browser-automation harvest
situations.definition: Drive a real browser session on the user's behalf to walk a provider's console and extract a credential, with a live action log and cancel.

situations.name: Local app and MCP discovery
situations.definition: Detect installed desktop apps or MCP servers on the machine and register them as connectors after a capability review.

situations.name: Grounding preview
situations.definition: Show the user which memories or documents the AI actually retrieved before answering.

situations.name: Feed grouping and collapse
situations.definition: A developer needs a chronological or categorical feed bucketed into collapsible groups.

situations.name: Device pairing ceremony
situations.definition: A developer needs a two-sided handshake between machines that survives event loss, is testable, and explains every refusal.

situations.name: Cross-process loop ownership
situations.definition: Deciding which of several processes sharing one local DB (windowed app, headless daemon, test instance) is allowed to run a singleton loop.

situations.name: Loop restart safety
situations.definition: Making sure starting or restarting the scheduler cannot leave a second live copy of every loop running against the same data.

situations.name: Release and version pipeline
situations.definition: A developer cuts a release and needs version files, tag, changelog, four platform builds, and updater artifacts to move together.

situations.name: Parallel session coordination
situations.definition: Multiple CLI agents share one checkout on one branch and need to not clobber each other's uncommitted work.

situations.name: Command input validation
situations.definition: A developer accepts a user-supplied id, name, or free-text field at the IPC boundary and needs the canonical whitelist/strip before it reaches SQL, a path, or storage.

situations.name: Page and section loading
situations.definition: Cover a lazy route or async data region while it warms without flashing an empty state.

situations.name: Page loading choreography
situations.definition: A developer needs a route or panel to go from cold to painted without blank gaps, skeleton blinks or re-ghosting.

situations.name: Definition list tables
situations.definition: Listing triggers / schedules / deployments / recipes with loading, empty, and filter states.

situations.name: Command palette entries
situations.definition: A developer wants a new destination, action, or setting to be reachable from Cmd+K.

situations.name: Git hook design
situations.definition: A developer wants a check to run automatically before commit or push without breaking the flow of concurrent CLI sessions sharing one tree.

situations.name: Engine ceilings and caps
situations.definition: A developer bounds a runaway loop, fan-out, batch, or spend and needs the constant plus the clamping helper in the right layer.

situations.name: Copy to clipboard
situations.definition: A developer needs a value copyable with confirmation feedback.

situations.name: Bulk re-run cohort
situations.definition: A developer needs to re-execute N past runs with bounded concurrency and report what got better, worse, or cost more.

situations.name: Drag-to-resize panel
situations.definition: A developer needs a splitter the user can drag to resize a terminal/panel, bounded and cleaned up.

situations.name: Mutating-query safe mode
situations.definition: Detect that a user-authored SQL statement mutates data and require a second confirmation before executing it.

situations.name: Remote resource scope picker
situations.definition: After connecting, let the user narrow a credential to specific remote resources fetched live from the provider, including dependent chains.

situations.name: Coverage matrix grid
situations.definition: Render an NxM crosstab where cell intensity communicates coverage and clicking a cell dispatches an action.

situations.name: Streaming chat transcript
situations.definition: Render a live, paginated message list that swaps a streaming placeholder for the persisted turn when it lands.

situations.name: Event chain timeline
situations.definition: A developer needs a vertical narrative of related events with a connecting spine.

situations.name: Schedule calendar
situations.definition: Laying fleet-wide schedule fires onto a week/month grid, distinguishing projected future fires from real past outcomes, and flagging overlaps.

situations.name: Section cold-load states
situations.definition: First-paint behaviour for async panels in these tabs — ghost rows, delayed skeletons, empty-vs-loading disambiguation.

situations.name: Layout document persistence
situations.definition: A developer needs spatial/board layout to survive restart, tolerate two writers, and migrate as the schema evolves.

situations.name: Cross-device job dispatch
situations.definition: Accepting and running work sent from another machine, deciding whether the sender is allowed to make you run anything.

situations.name: In-memory secret lifetime
situations.definition: A developer holds a plaintext secret in process memory and needs it zeroized, un-swappable, and non-printable in Debug output.

situations.name: Secret-leak scanning
situations.definition: A developer needs staged changes checked for credentials before they leave the machine, plus a way to triage historical hits.

situations.name: List entrance reveal
situations.definition: A developer wants rows/tiles to appear with a stagger the first time they arrive, without re-animating on every update.

situations.name: Settings key-value store
situations.definition: A developer persists a scalar app setting and needs one answer for its key, default, unit, and validation.

situations.name: Third-party API playground
situations.definition: Let the user browse a connector's endpoints, build a request with real auth, fire it, and read the response.

situations.name: Guided tour authoring
situations.definition: A developer adding a feature wants an in-app tour step that navigates to it, spotlights it, and completes when the user actually does the thing.

situations.name: Tier / build gating
situations.definition: A developer needs a feature to appear only for a given audience tier or build flavour.

situations.name: Streaming model output
situations.definition: Reading a model's NDJSON stream line by line, turning lines into typed events, and acting on them while the run is still in flight.

situations.name: SQL editor and result grid
situations.definition: Give the user a syntax-highlighted query editor plus a paged, typed result table against a live external database.

situations.name: Policy threshold settings card
situations.definition: Offer a small persisted settings card (toggle plus numeric bound) that pushes an operator policy live to the backend.

situations.name: Multi-condition status ladder
situations.definition: A developer needs a badge whose meaning depends on several fields evaluated in priority order, rendered at two or more densities.

situations.name: Shared fetch spine
situations.definition: A developer needs several surfaces to read the same backend bundle without each issuing its own duplicate fetch.

situations.name: Adoption checklist probes
situations.definition: A developer needs a setup or feature-discovery checklist whose completion reflects the user's real data, not just clicks.

situations.name: Definition flow visualization
situations.definition: Rendering a saved or generated automation as a read-only diagram/pipeline so a user can grasp its shape before adopting it.

situations.name: Catalog browse and compare
situations.definition: Searching a large definition catalog with structured/faceted filters and putting two or more candidates side by side before choosing.

situations.name: Connection pool and pragmas
situations.definition: A developer opens a pool against a SQLite file and needs consistent pragmas, timeouts, and hooks on every connection.

situations.name: Pre-flight dependency validation
situations.definition: Proving before a run starts that everything it needs — credentials, connectors, peer personas, capability contracts — actually exists.

situations.name: Crate layering discipline
situations.definition: A developer decides which workspace crate a new module belongs in so the dependency graph stays acyclic and rustc can parallelize.

situations.name: Supply-chain policy
situations.definition: A developer adds or bumps a dependency and needs the license, advisory, source-registry, and duplication policy applied.

situations.name: Windows loader and toolchain traps
situations.definition: A developer runs Rust tests or a build on Windows and hits a failure that is the loader or a mislabeled prebuilt artifact, not their code.

situations.name: Undo/redo over persisted operations
situations.definition: A developer needs Ctrl+Z to reverse an edit that has already been written to the backend, not just an in-memory state swap.

situations.name: Just-in-time auth prompt
situations.definition: Surface a mid-call authorization-required error as a consent URL the user can open, then retry the original operation.

situations.name: Composition autosave
situations.definition: Debounce-persist an in-progress editable document to an autosave slot while also supporting explicit save, save-as, open, and a recents list.

situations.name: Media lightbox viewer
situations.definition: Preview an image, video, or PDF full-screen with zoom, pan, rotate, and keyboard navigation across a set.

situations.name: Credential kill-switch
situations.definition: List every external consumer that has used a credential through the audited proxy and let the operator revoke one immediately.

situations.name: OS process reconciliation
situations.definition: Find processes the in-memory registry lost track of and let the user resume or kill them safely.

situations.name: Dead-letter triage
situations.definition: Reviewing events that failed terminally, clustering them by failure mode, and retrying or discarding them under a retry cap.

situations.name: Derived-state publication
situations.definition: A developer needs frontend-derived state that no backend query can reproduce to be readable by an agent or another surface.

situations.name: Tauri capability permissions
situations.definition: A developer uses a Tauri plugin API and must declare its permission in the right capability file for the right platforms.

situations.name: Content Security Policy scope
situations.definition: A developer adds a remote origin (image CDN, media stream, embed, telemetry endpoint) and must widen the webview CSP and asset-protocol scope for it.

situations.name: Route chunk loading
situations.definition: A developer lazy-loads a route/section and must cover the fetch-and-evaluate gap without a blank flash.

situations.name: Session delta digest
situations.definition: A developer needs a 'here is what happened while you were away' summary anchored on a last-seen watermark.

situations.name: Maintenance affordances
situations.definition: A developer needs dev-seed, garbage-collect and delete-all controls attached to a data surface.

situations.name: Tool invocation result contract
situations.definition: Returning a tool call's outcome in a shape callers, the audit log and the incidents inbox can all reason about, with output bounded.

situations.name: Deterministic verification and fix re-entry
situations.definition: Running a real check (tests, lint, exit code) after a model run and looping it back with the failure, bounded so it cannot spin.

situations.name: Live UI test automation
situations.definition: A developer wants an external driver to click through the real running desktop app rather than a mocked DOM.

situations.name: Locale bundle splitting
situations.definition: A developer needs translated strings to load as per-route lazy chunks instead of one 500KB bundle, without an English-first-paint flash.

situations.name: Adding a custom lint rule
situations.definition: A developer wants a repo convention machine-enforced in TS/TSX and needs to author, register, severity-tune, and test an ESLint rule.

situations.name: Chart rendering
situations.definition: A developer needs a chart that does not drag recharts into the initial bundle and matches the app's palette.

situations.name: Background completion notification
situations.definition: A developer must tell the user something they started finished, when they may have navigated away from the surface that started it.

situations.name: App-root modal host
situations.definition: Show a modal that must outlive the subtree that requested it, and let the caller await its outcome.

situations.name: Playback transport engine
situations.definition: Drive a play/pause/seek transport whose clock ticks many times a second without putting the time in React state.

situations.name: Route composer
situations.definition: An authoring surface for source→target wiring: arm a source, arm a target, set a run condition, then commit the pending link as a real backend object.

situations.name: Live event console
situations.definition: A continuously-updating stream view of system events with pause/resume buffering, a bounded window, and per-row detail.

situations.name: Multi-modal stack
situations.definition: Managing several stacked overlays from one surface without a useState pair per modal.

situations.name: Persisted settings contract
situations.definition: A developer adds a user-configurable app setting and needs its key, default, unit, and validation to have one canonical home.

situations.name: Agent-facing repo contract
situations.definition: A developer or agent needs to know this repo's canonical build/test/lint/scan commands and hard boundaries without reading prose.

situations.name: Codegen task registration
situations.definition: A developer adds a generated artifact and needs it to run on every dev/build without serializing the startup path or hanging it.

situations.name: Lazy chart loading
situations.definition: A developer needs Recharts to load off the critical path and to fail without taking the page down.

situations.name: Execution trace instrumentation
situations.definition: A developer adds a phase of work that should be attributable in the execution inspector with timing and cost.

situations.name: Detail modal
situations.definition: A developer needs a modal presenting one record in depth with actions.

situations.name: OCR extraction surface
situations.definition: Extract text from an image or PDF through a selectable backend, then preview, copy, or save the result.

situations.name: State-change desktop notification
situations.definition: Detect a backend entity crossing into a terminal state and raise an OS notification plus an in-app entry.

situations.name: Calendar heatmap
situations.definition: A developer needs a GitHub-style day-cell grid encoding activity intensity over a long window.

situations.name: Trace waterfall viewer
situations.definition: A developer needs nested spans rendered as a collapsible duration waterfall.

situations.name: Change capture and live updates
situations.definition: A developer wants a table's writes to reach the frontend live, or to be durably journaled for undo.

situations.name: Attention badge registry
situations.definition: A developer needs the count of things needing attention in a domain, consistent across sidebar, tabs and dashboards.

situations.name: Route chunk prefetch
situations.definition: A developer needs lazily-loaded routes and widgets to be warm before the user navigates.

situations.name: Build cache hygiene
situations.definition: A developer's local build gets slow, huge, or mysteriously broken, and needs the right surgical clean rather than a nuclear cargo clean.

situations.name: Guided setup instructions
situations.definition: Render provider setup docs as an interactive, resumable checklist with clickable links and persisted step completion.

situations.name: Readiness completion score
situations.definition: Derive a 0-100 'how set up is this' score from independent milestones and let the user jump to the weakest gap.

situations.name: Chart annotation overlay
situations.definition: A developer needs deploy, rotation and incident markers overlaid on a time-series chart.

situations.name: Drill-down shell
situations.definition: A developer needs a multi-level navigation surface (wall to project to group to detail) with breadcrumbs and preserved sub-tab state.

situations.name: Tauri config overlays
situations.definition: A developer needs a build variant (lite/stable/android) that differs from the canonical Tauri config in a controlled, minimal way.

situations.name: Bundle and binary size budget
situations.definition: A developer adds a dependency or asset and needs the shipped artifact to stay under a declared size ceiling.

situations.name: Design variant tab switcher
situations.definition: Scaffold several visual variants of a surface behind a small tab strip during active design iteration.

situations.name: API spec import
situations.definition: Accept an OpenAPI/Postman spec by file, paste, or catalog and merge its endpoints into an existing endpoint list.

situations.name: Theme customization
situations.definition: A developer needs the user to author a custom colour theme and know whether the result is readable.

situations.name: Pre-migration backup and recovery
situations.definition: A developer needs the user's database recoverable if the boot migration chain corrupts it.

situations.name: Documentation sync enforcement
situations.definition: A developer changes user-visible behavior and must update the feature doc, the onboarding tour, and the cross-repo marketing guide in the same session.

situations.name: Bulk translation pipeline
situations.definition: A developer has a translation gap across 13 locales and needs it closed without hand-editing 13 JSON files.

situations.name: Shared component boundary
situations.definition: A developer builds a reusable UI primitive and must decide whether it belongs in the catalog and keep it free of app state.

situations.name: Plugin enable gating
situations.definition: Turn a whole plugin on or off from a catalog and reflect that in the sidebar and nav.

situations.name: Marketplace feed wiring
situations.definition: Turning a subscribed external feed into a live listener on a persona.

situations.name: Search-entry contribution
situations.definition: A developer wants their feature's toggles and destinations reachable from the global command palette.

situations.name: Theme contrast enforcement
situations.definition: A developer adds or edits a color token and needs every theme's text pairings to still clear WCAG AA.

situations.name: Conventional commit format
situations.definition: A developer writes a commit message that the changelog generator and release tooling can parse.
